v1_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610/month Jun to 1180-1260/month Aug-Sep, E-05). A confirmed contributing mechanism: manual-read route completion fell to 88% against a 95% target for 9200 accounts over Aug-Sep (E-01), pushing more accounts onto estimate substitution, which accounts for 41% (1240/3025) of currently disputed bills (E-03). Tariff changes (E-02) and dispute-handling capacity (E-04, within SLA) are ruled out as causes, but this estimate-substitution mechanism does not yet explain the majority (59%, 1785/3025) of disputed bills, which used ACTUAL reads (E-03) — a second, unconfirmed billing-pipeline mechanism is driving most of the surge.
v2_problem: Dispute ticket volume roughly doubled since August 2026 (610/590 per month Jun/Jul to 1180/1260 Aug/Sep, E-05), driven by billing-import validation rule BV-17 (deployed 2026-08-01, E-12), which compares raw AMI register values to 12-month m3 consumption history with no unit scaling. Because AMI meters on firmware v4.2 (rolled out June 2026, E-13) report register values in 0.1 m3 instead of m3, BV-17 systematically misflags high consumption at import. This is confirmed for the ESTIMATED-read channel, where 1184 of 1240 disputed bills had a valid AMI read rejected by billing import for high consumption rather than lacking a read at all (E-11); because BV-17 applies at import regardless of read channel (E-12), the same mechanism plausibly also explains disputes on the dominant ACTUAL-read channel (59%, 1785/3025, E-03). Tariff changes (E-02, E-06) and ticket-handling capacity (E-04, within SLA) are ruled out as causes.
